diagnoses: Unresponsive patient after anesthesia (four possible causes)
presentations: unresponsive in the postanesthesia care unit
brief: A patient is unresponsive in the postanesthesia recovery unit, with the same front story but four possible causes across four scenarios. Learners explore diagnoses and practice care across the perioperative period.

learners: neurology and emergency residents, medical students, nurses
brief: A patient with acute stroke symptoms is portrayed by a standardized patient. Learners run a stroke code, use the NIH Stroke Scale, and make time-critical treatment decisions as team leaders.

learners: emergency, internal medicine and family medicine residents
brief: A patient arrives after an unknown ingestion that proves to be a cardiotoxic calcium channel blocker. Learners practice exam, clinical reasoning, and treatment of the poisoning and its complications.

A critically ill infant with bronchiolitis presents to the emergency department. Learners practice recognizing severe illness and managing it with high flow nasal cannula oxygen and other support, using a manikin.
A child arrives with blunt abdominal trauma at risk of shock or bowel injury. Learners practice rapid assessment, resuscitation, airway decisions, and arranging definitive care.

presentations: family meeting about change in patient condition
brief: An SP plays an upset family member of a hospitalized patient across several meetings as the patient's condition changes. Students practice breaking bad news and are assessed on milestones.

diagnoses: Airway obstruction from mucus plug in prone position
presentations: loss of end tidal CO2 and ventilation during spine surgery
brief: A 42-year-old male smoker having spinal surgery in the prone position suddenly has complete airway obstruction. Learners practice diagnosis, management, and crisis resource management.

diagnoses: Critical medical condition requiring transfer to acute care
presentations: deterioration needing hand-off from clinic to hospital
brief: An SP with a common critical medical condition moves from an ambulatory setting to acute care. Interprofessional student teams practice triage, recognizing the need for transfer, and hand-off communication.

presentations: altered mental status in a toddler
brief: A 2-year-old has altered mental status from cerebral sinovenous thrombosis after iron deficiency anemia and dehydration. Actors follow scripts while learners examine the child and work through a rare diagnosis.

diagnoses: Early and late stage breast cancer
presentations: breast cancer prevention, diagnosis and treatment
brief: Small groups discuss short answer patient cases on breast cancer. Learners practice decisions on prevention, diagnosis and treatment across early and late disease.
Five OSCE stations cover delivering bad news, error disclosure, informed consent, and surgical and medical health care disparities. Residents are scored on communication by trained SPs.
Scott Green is a patient who had a heart attack and is now depressed. Students take a chronic disease history and practice recognizing and treating depression.

diagnoses: Spiritual and religious influences on care
brief: Two case studies and two role plays let students practice taking a spiritual history. They learn how to ask about religious beliefs and practices and use the answers in care.

presentations: cognitive and mood changes in an older adult
learners: internal medicine residents, pharmacy residents, psychology students
brief: Interprofessional teams work through a geriatric patient case with dementia, depression and delirium. They practice prioritizing evaluation and treatment among competing diagnoses.

presentations: need for IV access in a child
brief: A child with difficult intravenous access needs an IV placed. Learners practice handling the situation in a repeatable, observable simulation.

diagnoses: Threatened preterm birth at the limit of viability
brief: An SP plays a parent in an antenatal consultation at the limit of viability. Trainees practice communication and apply ethical principles when discussing options.

diagnoses: Unexpected congenital malformation in a newborn
presentations: birth of an infant with a malformation
brief: An SP plays a parent after the birth of an infant with an unexpected malformation. Trainees practice communication and ethical reasoning about intensive care versus palliative care.
A young adult SP presents with acute sore throat. Students interview the patient, write a SOAP note, and receive feedback from the SP, peers and faculty.
Denise or Dennis Jones is an SP with a mood disorder and suicidal thoughts. Students practice history taking and suicide risk assessment during the psychiatry clerkship.

learners: pediatric anesthesiologists, nuclear medicine and radiology providers
brief: A child with newly diagnosed lymphoma needs a combined PET/CT scan for staging. Learners discuss safe and effective anesthesia care while minimizing radiation exposure.
A patient with autonomic failure is presented as a full case with instructor and student guides. Students explain baroreflex regulation of blood pressure and apply it in follow-up mini-cases.

presentations: death of a child in the emergency department
brief: An SP plays a parent who must be told that their child has died. Interns practice the communication skills of a death disclosure.

diagnoses: Critical incident such as medical error or unanticipated death
brief: A workshop includes an SP encounter where trainees disclose a critical incident to a patient or family. They practice honest, compassionate, collaborative communication and complete a documentation exercise.
A patient in labor develops shoulder dystocia. Obstetric, nursing and anesthesia providers practice a coordinated team response to deliver the baby quickly.
Six high-fidelity cases present acute critical care problems, each with protocol, labs, imaging and teaching notes. Interns practice decision making under time pressure.
A child in the emergency setting has thyroid storm. Learners practice recognizing it and starting management using a manikin, with a focus on team communication.

exclude_reason: Team conflict role-play, no patient case

presentations: child in cardiac arrest after suspected abuse
brief: A child dies in the emergency department from non-accidental trauma. Teams practice a pediatric code and navigate the emotionally charged event, including communication.
Twelve casualties from a bomb blast are played by seven high-fidelity simulators and five SPs. Residents practice triage and care of multiple patients, including amputations and severe hemorrhage.
A child has a traumatic brain injury with risk of hypoxia, hypotension and herniation. Learners practice stabilization and transfer to a pediatric trauma center, with a team communication focus.
A 13-station, case-based OSCE with 5 minutes per station tests clinical knowledge. Two stations are interactive, with faculty playing parents.
Two multimedia cases cover acute and chronic hyponatremia, one with an interactive treatment simulation. Learners practice reasoning and managing electrolyte disorders.
A standardized mother brings her 4-month-old, a doll, for routine preventive care. Students interview and advise her within a time-limited encounter.
A child with neuromuscular scoliosis has a cardiac arrest from unrecognized hemorrhage during prone spinal fusion. Learners build a differential, communicate a plan, and mobilize resources.

presentations: decision making about a critically ill infant
brief: An SP plays a parent of a severely ill infant in the NICU. Trainees practice communication and ethical decision making about treatment.
A 40-year-old man has signs of organophosphate poisoning. Learners recognize the toxidrome, select protective equipment and treat in a manikin-based emergency department scenario.

brief: Interprofessional teams work through a case of a patient with chronic pain in an urban primary care setting. They practice collaborative care planning.

diagnoses: Adverse reaction to epinephrine in cardiovascular disease
presentations: respiratory and cardiovascular distress in the dental office
brief: Three videos show dental patients with a severe allergic reaction, an adverse drug reaction in a man with cardiovascular disease, and near-syncope after a procedure. Students link physiology to medical emergencies in the dental office.

learners: internal medicine residents and medical students
brief: Three to four OSCE stations give a disease-specific history for neck and spine problems. Residents practice a hypothesis-driven musculoskeletal exam, with volunteer students and faculty supporting the stations.
Four SP cases present sensitive obstetric situations. Students practice and refine communication skills, then reflect on their strengths and weaknesses.

diagnoses: Code status discussion with hospitalized patient
brief: Residents role-play code status discussions with a hospitalized patient after a faculty demonstration. They practice a risk and benefit framework and respond to patient emotions.

diagnoses: Autonomic dysreflexia in spinal cord injury
presentations: rehabilitation emergency in a spinal cord-injured patient
brief: An SP plays a spinal cord-injured patient in autonomic dysreflexia, a rehabilitation emergency. Residents practice recognizing and managing it in 15-minute encounters.
Rosa is an edentulous older patient in an interactive virtual case. Students link oral health, nutrition and counseling while answering questions.

learners: medical students, residents, pharmacy and psychology learners
brief: Interprofessional teams take a readiness test, then apply obesity knowledge to case-based problems. They practice assessing biopsychosocial factors and planning treatment.

diagnoses: Hydrofluoric acid burn with systemic toxicity
brief: A patient arrives at a community emergency department after skin exposure to hydrofluoric acid. Learners practice decontamination, checking electrolytes and ECG, and giving IV calcium to prevent cardiovascular collapse.

diagnoses: Post-hospital care transition in an older adult
presentations: first primary care visit after hospitalization
brief: Mr. John Coleman, an older patient, attends his first outpatient visit after hospital discharge with a caregiver, shown on video. Trainees practice interdisciplinary care transitions.

Two sequences of pediatric resuscitation scenarios use high-fidelity mannequins. Teams repeat progressively harder rounds with directive feedback to practice resuscitation for PEA and ventricular tachycardia.

diagnoses: Typhoid fever presenting as heat stroke
brief: A traveler presents with typhoid fever that looks like heat stroke. Learners practice resuscitation and recognition of a travel-related illness, with or without high-fidelity equipment.
An SP presents with diarrhea. Students interview and examine the patient, write a SOAP note, and receive feedback from the SP, peers and faculty.

diagnoses: Emergency department cases with hidden urgent diagnoses
brief: Five emergency department cases each lead toward an obvious diagnosis while subtle cues suggest a more urgent one. Learners practice spotting cognitive biases and considering alternatives.

diagnoses: Common obstetric and gynecologic paging problems
brief: Students receive pages about eight obstetric and gynecologic patient problems, such as postoperative tachycardia and postpartum pain. They practice deciding how to respond, then debrief.
A child has respiratory distress from croup. Learners practice acute and emergent management using a script, props and a high-fidelity mannequin, with an evaluation tool.

learners: medical students on the obstetrics and gynecology clerkship
brief: Two clinical patient cases cover endometrial hyperplasia and cervical dysplasia. After preclass videos, students discuss evaluation and management of each precancerous condition.

learners: medical students, nurse practitioner and physician assistant trainees
brief: Denise is a virtual patient presenting for an initial psychiatric evaluation. Learners practice a psychiatric interview and mental status exam with immediate feedback.

diagnoses: Neck pain with possible spinal cord compression
brief: A 65-year-old patient with neck pain presents to the emergency department. In a 15-minute SP OSCE, the examinee takes a history, builds a differential, interprets tests, and defends a final diagnosis.

Student groups manage a dehydrated child's fluids and electrolytes from hospital admission through discharge. They practice pediatric fluid and electrolyte management after a flipped classroom preparation.

diagnoses: Geriatric syndromes in older adults with HIV
brief: Topical cases cover common geriatric syndromes in older patients with HIV, with questions and answers for instructors. Learners practice evidence-based management of multiple age-related conditions.

diagnoses: Adrenal insufficiency with shock in an infant
learners: health care professionals in emergency care
brief: An infant presents to the pediatric emergency department in uncompensated shock from adrenal insufficiency, based on an actual case. Learners recognize the signs and stabilize using pediatric advanced life support.

Three student-led simulation cases cover a basic disease process and stabilization of a life-threatening arrhythmia. Each has learning goals and outcome checklists.
Student teams work through case vignettes with history and clinical photos showing skin signs of systemic disease. They practice piecing together a diagnosis from a changing clinical picture.
Small groups review clinical cases of pulmonary infection and identify the two most likely pathogens from setting, history and exam. They then teach each other in a jigsaw format.

learners: residents, fellows and other care providers
brief: A patient has an acute pit viper envenomation with local tissue injury and systemic effects. The package has a case narrative with branch points, and learners practice managing the injury.
An SP portrays a 41-year-old woman with recurrent nausea and vomiting. Students interview and examine her, write a SOAP note, and receive feedback.

A problem-based learning case follows a patient with lung adenocarcinoma from misleading initial presentation through workup, treatment, relapse and end-of-life issues. Students study it in small groups over three sessions.

presentations: patient with something stuck in the airway

learners: emergency medicine residents, paramedics, residents and medical students
brief: A standardized patient presents with a snake bite to the hand and a photo of the snake. Learners identify a rattlesnake envenomation and manage it through several branch points.

presentations: death of a patient in the emergency department
brief: An SP plays the spouse of a patient who has died. Interns deliver a death disclosure and receive feedback from the SP, faculty and a peer.

exclude_reason: Patient safety curriculum, no single case

brief: A pregnant patient is at risk of preterm birth. Students take a history and exam on a high-fidelity mannequin, interpret a fetal heart rate tracing, and develop a management plan.
A nurse pages the learner about a patient with an infected central venous catheter. The learner practices medical decision making and communication in a single-station SP case.
Residents meet family members of a critically ill ICU patient in a simulation session. They practice answering urgent questions, responding to distress, and discussing goals of care.

presentations: triage in a busy pediatric emergency department
brief: Case-based scenarios place learners in a pediatric emergency department with limited time, information and resources. They practice triage, prioritizing and clinical reasoning.
Two inpatient cases are shown on video with simulated patients: a woman with mania in bipolar disorder and a young woman with major depression. Student teams analyze the cases and discuss them.

presentations: acute management of DKA in a child
brief: A short module gives DKA management guidelines and a case scenario with three questions. Providers practice the immediate care of a child with DKA.

learners: emergency medicine acting interns and residents
brief: A patient has acute synthetic cannabinoid toxicity in a high-fidelity simulation. Learners in assigned team roles practice recognizing and treating agitation, psychosis and cardiac effects.
A self-learning module follows a patient with dementia on video from presentation to five-year follow-up. Students practice differential diagnosis and treatment planning with quizzes.
Student teams apply cholesterol treatment guidelines to clinical case scenarios. They practice rational prescribing to reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.

learners: medical students, emergency residents, pediatric emergency fellows
brief: A patient has an acute tricyclic antidepressant overdose. The package has a case narrative with branch points, and learners test and apply their management of this life-threatening ingestion.
A self-learning module shows a patient with a personality disorder on video from presentation through three years of follow-up. Students practice differential diagnosis and treatment.

presentations: patient on warfarin with bleeding or high INR
brief: Team-based application exercises present patients on warfarin who have bleeding, possible bleeding, or a high INR. Learners practice managing anticoagulation safely.
An SP with a mock arm abscess needs incision and drainage. Learners practice aseptic technique and communication with the SP and a mock nurse, using a checklist.
Team-based learning with case-based questions covers allergic rhinitis, sinusitis and pharyngitis in primary care. Residents practice diagnosis and treatment.

presentations: emotional and clinical care after pregnancy loss
brief: The curriculum includes case vignettes with standardized patients on pregnancy loss. Students practice sensitive communication with women and families.

diagnoses: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome after Norwood repair
presentations: infant needing laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication and gastrostomy
brief: A neonate with hypoplastic left heart syndrome after Norwood repair has feeding difficulties and needs surgery. Learners discuss the anesthetic challenges of this real clinical case.

presentations: fall with hip fracture in a terminally ill patient
brief: A 78-year-old woman with metastatic cancer arrives with a hip fracture after a fall and decompensates from a massive pulmonary embolism. Learners practice emergency care combined with palliative medicine.

diagnoses: Adrenal crisis from abrupt steroid withdrawal
presentations: hypotension unresponsive to fluids and pressors
brief: A patient with hypotension that does not respond to fluids has stopped chronic steroids for sarcoid. Residents practice getting the key history, recognizing adrenal crisis and starting treatment, with actors playing family and staff.

diagnoses: Hyperkalemia from salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia
presentations: critical potassium level in an infant
brief: An infant with congenital adrenal hyperplasia has salt-wasting with critical hyperkalemia. Learners practice recognizing it and stabilizing the cardiac membranes to prevent ventricular arrhythmias.

diagnoses: Kidney injury and drug toxicity in older adults
brief: An OSCE covers kidney injury and drug toxicity in aging patients. Fellows practice medication and renal dosing decisions and are scored with a checklist, followed by faculty debriefing.

Three simulations use a standard actor and a 3-D dental mold to show dental injury, ankyloglossia, and tongue thrusting. Paired students combine findings with the patient's description to assess and plan care.

diagnoses: Sensitive pelvic exam and Pap test
presentations: routine pelvic exam in a patient with trauma history
brief: An SP who is lesbian and has a trauma history needs a pelvic exam and Pap test. Residents practice a sensitive and technically sound exam and receive formative feedback.

diagnoses: New atorvastatin prescription after myocardial infarction
brief: An inquisitive, educated SP is started on atorvastatin after a heart attack. Students counsel on indication, mechanism, side effects and food and drug interactions.

presentations: ingested foreign body in a child
learners: emergency medicine residents and pediatric emergency fellows
brief: A child has swallowed a button battery lodged in the esophagus. Learners recognize it from radiograph features and practice arranging immediate removal.
An SP with PTSD has a flashback during a 20-minute inpatient encounter. Learners recognize an impending attack and offer ways to interrupt it.

diagnoses: Critical aortic coarctation in a neonate
brief: A neonate arrives in extremis from a previously undetected critical aortic coarctation. Learners stabilize with oxygen, fluids and warming, give prostaglandin, manage the airway, and involve cardiology.
Team-based exercises present head trauma patients with imaging studies. Residents practice a systematic approach to reading the images for specific clinical questions.
A patient has ingested ethylene glycol, an uncommon life-threatening poisoning. The package has a case narrative with branch points, and learners practice recognition and treatment.

learners: pediatric fellows in critical care, cardiology, oncology and neonatology
brief: Three simulated scenarios with debriefing cover palliative care, end-of-life care, and difficult communication in pediatrics. Fellows practice high-stakes conversations and pain and symptom management.

A child develops significant bronchospasm during a general anesthetic. Trainees practice recognizing and managing the physiologic effects in a repeatable simulation with instructor and debriefing guides.

Student teams act as attending physicians and rotate through three stations of primary care scenarios, including urgent issues and patient phone calls. They record assessments and plans, then debrief.
A patient with cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with a variceal bleed. Student groups manage the patient in a high-fidelity simulation over two rounds, then debrief.
Cases follow patients with shoulder, elbow, and wrist or hand pain from initial presentation to surgical intervention. Students practice the clinical workup with an internist and orthopedic surgeon.

diagnoses: Hypertension referred from dentist to primary care
presentations: elevated blood pressure found at a dental visit
learners: students in dentistry, medicine, pharmacy, nursing, social work and dietetics
brief: Interprofessional student teams plan coordinated care for a patient with hypertension referred to primary care from the dentist. They practice team huddles and designing a shared care plan.

diagnoses: Hemorrhage as a complication of uterine aspiration
presentations: bleeding after miscarriage or abortion procedure
brief: A uterine aspiration case is complicated by hemorrhage. Learners use the 6 Ts mnemonic to work through causes and management, practicing on a fruit model in provider, assistant and evaluator roles.

diagnoses: Psychosocial stress in an LGBT youth
brief: Nathan or Natalie Marquez is a 15 to 25 year old SP with headache who has conflicted feelings about sexual orientation and family pressure. Students take a full history and recognize how psychosocial stress can appear as physical complaints.
A premature newborn has a tracheoesophageal fistula and hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Learners work through complex physiology and competing anesthetic goals in a case-based exercise.

presentations: critical event in the operating room
brief: Eight high-fidelity scenarios each simulate a perioperative critical event, with patient history, exam and labs. Teams practice management with and without a critical event checklist.

learners: medical students entering pediatric, medicine-pediatrics and family medicine residencies
brief: Four pediatric cases support role-play on writing assessments and plans, prioritizing tasks, answering pages, and handing off patients. Learners practice these intern skills and reinforce clinical management.

diagnoses: Pediatric upper airway foreign body obstruction
presentations: near-complete upper airway obstruction in an infant
brief: An infant arrives with near-complete upper airway obstruction from a foreign body, based on a real case. Learners practice recognizing it and performing transtracheal jet ventilation.

presentations: adverse drug reaction in a clinic patient
brief: A covert SP in a working clinic has medication-induced QT prolongation. Students identify the adverse drug reaction, plan medication changes, educate the patient and present to the attending.

Four pediatric radiology on-call scenarios use standardized participants and a mannequin. Residents practice diagnosis, management, parent consent, education and consultation with an emergency physician.
